starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.player: Do you have any other quests for me to do?

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: Nothing I can think of at the moment...
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Recruitment Drive quest.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Quests, eh? Well, I don't have anything on the go at the moment, but there is an organisation that is always looking for capable adventurers to assist them.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Your excellent work sorting out those Black Knights means I will happily write you a letter of recommendation.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze.text: Would you like me to put your name forwards to them?

steps.player: Sure thing Sir Amik, sign me up!

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: Erm, well, this is a little embarrassing, I already HAVE put you forward as a potential member.

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: They are called the Temple Knights, and you are to meet Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador park for testing immediately.

steps.player: Okey dokey, I'll go do that then.
No thanks, that doesn't sound like the kind of thing that would interest me...

steps.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
steps.text: As you wish adventurer, let's say no more about it.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.player: Do you have any other quests for me to do?

starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.speaker: Sir Amik Varze
starting-out-talking-to-sir-amik-varze-t.text: No, I am afraid not. I suggest you go meet Sir Tiffy in Falador Park, he will be expecting you.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.player: Sir Amik Varze sent me to meet you here for some sort of testing...?

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Ah, [player name]! Amik told me all about you, dontchaknow! Spiffing job you did with the old Black Knights there, absolutely first class.

starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-out-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Well, a top-notch fellow like yourself is just the right sort we've been seeking for our organisation.

steps.player: ...testing? What exactly do you mean by testing?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Jolly bad show! Varze was supposed to have informed you about all this before sending you here!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, not your fault I suppose, what? Anywho, our organisation is looking for a certain specific type of person to join.

steps.player: So... You want me to go kill some monster or something for you?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Not at all, old bean. There's plenty of warriors around should we require dumb muscle.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: That's really not the kind of thing our organisation is after, what?

steps.player: So you want me to go and fetch you some kind of common item, and then take it for delivery somewhere on the other side of the country?
Because I really hate doing that!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Haw haw haw What a dull thing to ask of someone, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I know what you mean though, I did my fair share of running errands when I was a young adventurer, myself!

steps.player: So what exactly will this test consist of?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Can't let just any old riff-raff in, what? The mindless thugs and bully boys are best left in the White Knights or the Guards, we look for the top-shelf brains to join us.

steps.player: So you want to test my brains?  Will it hurt?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Haw Haw Haw That's a good one!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Not in the slightest... Well, maybe a bit, but we all have to make sacrifices occasionally, what?

steps.player: What do you want me to do then?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: It's a test of wits, what? I'll take you to our secret training grounds, and you will have to pass through a series of five separate intelligence tests to prove you're our sort of

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: adventurer.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Standard puzzle room rules will apply.

steps.player: Erm... what are 'standard  puzzle room rules' exactly?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Never done this sort of thing before, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: The simple rules are: No items or equipment to be brought with you. Each room is a self contained puzzle. You may quit at any time.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Of course, if you quit a room, then all your progress up to that point will be cleared, and you'll have to start again from scratch.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Our organisation manages to filter all the top-notch adventurers this way. So, are you ready to go?

steps.player: This organisation you keep mentioning... Perhaps you could tell me a little about it?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oh, that Amik! Jolly bad form, did he not tell you anything that he was supposed to?

steps.player: No... He didn't really tell me anything except to come here and meet you...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well now old sport, let me give you the heads up and the low down, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I represent the Temple Knights. We are the premier order of Knights in Asgarnia, if not the world. Saradomin himself personally founded our order

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: centuries ago, and we answer only to him.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Only the very best of the best are permitted to join, and the powers we command are formidable indeed.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: You might say that we are the front line of defence for the entire kingdom!

steps.player: So what's the difference between you and the White Knights?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, in simple terms, we're better! Any fool with a sword can manage to get into the White Knights, which is mostly the reason they are so very, very incompetent, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: The Temple Knights on the other hand have to be smarter, stronger, better than all others. We are the elite. No man controls us for our orders come directly from

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Saradomin himself!

steps.player: Cool, you mean I get to meet Saradomin?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, uh, not exactly... Sir Vey Lance, our head of operations, is the only one of our order who has ever personally met Saradomin, but everything he tells us to do is done with

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Saradomin's implicit permission.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: It's not every job where you have more authority than the king, now is it?

steps.player: Wait... You can order the King around?!?!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, not me personally, I'm only in the recruitment side of things dontchaknow, but the higher ranking members of the organisation have almost absolute power over this kingdom.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Plus a few others, so I hear....

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Anyway, this is why we keep our organisation shrouded in secrecy, and why we demand such rigorous testing for all potential recruits. Speaking of which, are you ready to begin your

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: testing?

steps.player: Yeah, this sounds right up my street. Let's go!

steps.text: If the player does not have an empty inventory or has equipped items:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, bad luck old [boy/gal/bean], you'll need to have a completely empty inventory and you can't be wearing any equipment before we can accurately test you.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Don't want people cheating by smuggling stuff in, what?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Come and see me again after you've been to the old bank to drop your stuff off, what?
If the player has an empty inventory and no equipped items:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Jolly good show! Now, the training grounds location is a secret so...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Here we go! Mind your head!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oops, ignore the smell! Nearly there!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: And... Here we are! Best of luck!

steps.player: Well... I don't know... This doesn't really sound like my kind of thing...
To be honest, I'd rather go kill stuff for loot than use my mind to work things out...

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, it takes all sorts to make the world spin, what? Maybe you'll find a nice job with the Guards sometime.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Sad though, your intelligence file seemed quite promising. Should you change your mind, you come back and let me know, what?

the-tests-upon-failing-a-test.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-tests-upon-failing-a-test.text: Oh, jolly bad luck, what? Not quite the brainbox you thought you were, eh?

the-tests-upon-failing-a-test.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-tests-upon-failing-a-test.text: Well, never mind! You have an open invitation to join our organisation, so when you're feeling a little smarter, come back and talk to me again!

the-tests-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashien-a.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-tests-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashien-a.text: Ah, what ho! Back for another go at the old testing, what?

the-tests-sir-ren-itchood-entering-the-r.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
the-tests-sir-ren-itchood-entering-the-r.text: Greetings friend, and welcome here, you'll find my puzzle not so clear. Hidden amongst my words, it's true, the password for the door as a clue.

options.text: Can I have the clue for the door?

steps.text: If the answer is word 1:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Better than me, you'll not find In rhyming and in puzzles. This clue so clear will tax your mind Entirely as it confuzzles!
If the answer is word 2:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: This riddle of mine may confuse, I am quite sure of that. Mayhap you should closely peruse Every word i have spat?
If the answer is word 3:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Feel the aching of your mind In puzzlement, confused. See the clue hidden behind His words, as you perused.
If the answer is word 4:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: More than words, i have not for you Except the things i say today. Aware are you, this is a clue? Take note of what i say!
If the answer is word 5:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Look closely at the words i speak; And study closely every part. See for yourself the word you seek Trapped for you if you're smart.
If the answer is word 6:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Rare it is that you will see A puzzle such as this! In many ways it tickles me Now, watching you hit and miss!

options.text: Can I have a different clue?

steps.player: I don't get that riddle...
Can I have a different one?

steps.text: If the answer is word 1:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Before you hurry through that door Inspect the words i spoke. There is a simple hidden flaw Ere you think my rhyme a joke.
If the answer is word 2:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Twice it is now, i have stated In a rhyme, what is the pass. Maybe my words obfuscated Entirely beyond your class.
If the answer is word 3:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: First my clue you did not see, I really wish you had. Such puzzling wordplay devilry Has left you kind of mad!
If the answer is word 4:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Many types have passed through here Even such as you amongst their sort. And in the end, the puzzles clear; The hidden word you saught.
If the answer is word 5:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Last time my puzzle did not help Apparently, so you've bidden. Study my speech carefully, whelp To find the answer, hidden.
If the answer is word 6:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Repetition, once again Against good sense it goes. In my words, the answers plain Now that you see rhyme flows.

options.text: Can I have the clue for the door?
Can I have the final clue?

steps.player: I don't get that riddle...
Can I have the final clue for the door?

steps.text: If the answer is word 1:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Betrayed by words the answer is In that what i say is the key There is no more help after this Especially no more from me.
If the answer is word 2:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Three times now, my riddle said; I hope you finally see the clue. Maybe think on what you've read; Easy when you know what to do.
If the answer is word 3:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: For the last time i will state In simple words, the clue. Such tricky words make you irate Having no idea what to do...
If the answer is word 4:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Maybe i will do my best; Especially at giving clues. Attempt to help you pass the test! That should help me pay my dues.
If the answer is word 5:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Lo! my final speech is now Attended to by you. Study my words, and find out how To understand my clue!
If the answer is word 6:

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Repeat myself to give the clue Again, i now do speak. It's hidden in my words - hey you! Now find the answer you seek.

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: Your wit is sharp, your brains quite clear; You solved my puzzle with no fear. At puzzles I rank you quite the best, now enter the portal for your next test.

steps.speaker: Sir Ren Itchood
steps.text: It's sad to say, this test beat you. I'll send you to Tiffy, what to do?
You have failed to solve the riddle.

the-tests-ms-hynn-terprett-entering-the-.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
the-tests-ms-hynn-terprett-entering-the-.text: Greetings, [player name]. I am here to test your wits with a simple riddle.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Here is my riddle: I estimate there to be 1 million inhabitants in the world of Gielinor, creatures and people both.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: What would be the number you would get if you multiply the number of fingers on everythings left hand, to the nearest million?
Enter amount:

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Here is my riddle: I have both a husband and daughter.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: My husband is four times older than my daughter. In twenty years time, he will be twice as old as my daughter.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: How old is my daughter now?
Enter amount:

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Here is my riddle: Which of the following statements is true?

steps.prompt: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The number of false statements here is one
The number of false statements here is two
The number of false statements here is three.
The number of false statements here is four.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Here is my riddle: Imagine that you have been captured by an enemy. You are to be killed, but in a moment of mercy, the enemy has allowed you to pick your own demise.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Your first choice is to be drowned in a lake of acid.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Your second choice is to be burned on a fire.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Your third choice is to be thrown to a pack of wolves that have not been fed in over a month.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Your final choice of fate is to be thrown from the walls of a castle, many hundreds of feet high.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Which fate would you be wise to choose?

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Here is my riddle: I dropped four identical stones, into four identical buckets, each containing an identical amount of water.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: The first bucket's water was at 32 degrees Fahrenheit, the second was at 33 degrees, the third at 34 and the fourth was at 35 degrees.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Which bucket's stone dropped to the bottom of the bucket last?

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: Excellent work, [player name]. Please step through the portal to meet your next challenge.

steps.speaker: Ms. Hynn Terprett
steps.text: No... I am very sorry. Apparently you are not up to the challenge. I will return you where you came from, better luck in the future.
(Continues with failure dialogue.)

the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.text: Welcome, [player name]. This room will test your observation skills.

the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.text: Study the statues closely. There is one missing statue in this room.

the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.text: We will also mix the order up a little to make things interesting for you!

the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-entering-the-room.text: You have 10 seconds to memorise the statues... starting NOW!

the-tests-lady-table-after-waiting-10-se.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-after-waiting-10-se.text: We will now dim the lights and bring the missing statue back in.

the-tests-lady-table-after-waiting-10-se.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-after-waiting-10-se.text: Please touch the statue you think has been added.

the-tests-lady-table-talking-to-lady-tab.player: What am I supposed to be doing again?

the-tests-lady-table-talking-to-lady-tab.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-talking-to-lady-tab.text: Touch the statue that was brought in after you entered.

the-tests-lady-table-talking-to-lady-tab.speaker: Lady Table
the-tests-lady-table-talking-to-lady-tab.text: If you touch the wrong one, you will fail this task, and will be escorted back to Falador.

steps.speaker: Lady Table
steps.text: Excellent work, [player name]. Please step through the portal to meet your next challenge.

steps.speaker: Lady Table
steps.text: No... I am very sorry. Apparently you are not up to the challenge. I will return you where you came from, better luck in the future.

the-tests-sir-tinley-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Tinley
the-tests-sir-tinley-entering-the-room.text: Ah, [player name], you have arrived. Speak to me to begin your task.

the-tests-sir-tinley-talking-to-sir-tinl.speaker: Sir Tinley
the-tests-sir-tinley-talking-to-sir-tinl.text: Ah, welcome [player name]. I have but one clue for you to pass this room's puzzle: 'Patience'.

the-tests-sir-tinley-interacting-with-an.speaker: Sir Tinley
the-tests-sir-tinley-interacting-with-an.text: No... I am very sorry. Apparently you are not up to the challenge. I will return you where you came from, better luck in the future.

the-tests-sir-tinley-after-completing-th.speaker: Sir Tinley
the-tests-sir-tinley-after-completing-th.text: Excellent work, [player name]. Please step through the portal to meet your next challenge.

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-entering-the.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-entering-the.text: Ah, [player name], you're finally here. Your task for this room is to defeat Sir Leye. He has been blessed by Saradomin to be undefeatable by any blade, so it should be quite a challenge for you.

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-entering-the.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-entering-the.text: If you are having problems, remember; A true warrior uses his wits as much as his brawn. Fight smarter, not harder.

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-talking-to-s.speaker: Sir Leye
the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-talking-to-s.text: AH-HA HA HA! You can NEVER defeat ME! I am blessed by Saradomin himself! NO BLADE MAY DEFEAT ME!

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-defeating-si.text: If the player has completed 1-3 rooms:

steps.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
steps.text: Excellent work, [player name]. Please step through the portal to meet your next challenge.

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-defeating-si.text: If the player has completed 4 rooms:

steps.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
steps.text: Well done, that was your fourth test, you only have one more to go.

steps.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
steps.text: Please step through the portal to your final test... ...and good luck, [player name].

the-tests-sir-kuam-ferentse-defeating-si.text: If the player has completed 5 rooms:

steps.speaker: Sir Kuam Ferentse
steps.text: Excellent work! You have passed all five of the required tests! Please accept my congratulations!

the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.text: Greetings, [player name]. Welcome to my challenge.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.text: All you need to do is leave from the opposite door to where you came in by.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.text: I will warn you that this is more complicated than it may at first appear.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-entering-the-roo.text: I should also warn you that there are limited supplies of the items in this room, so think carefully before using them, or you may find yourself stuck, and have to leave to start again!

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.player: Can you give me any help?

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: No, I am sorry, but that is forbidden by our rules.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: If you are having a particularly tough time of it, I suggest you leave and come back later when you are in a more receptive frame of mind.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: Sometimes a break from concentration will yield fresh insight. Our aim is to test you, but not to the point of frustration!

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.player: Please... I am REALLY stuck... Isn't there ANYTHING you can do to help me...?

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: Well... Look, I really shouldn't say anything about this room, but...

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: When I was attempting to join the Temple Knights I myself had to do this puzzle myself.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: It was slightly different, but the idea behind it was the same, and I left the notes I had made while doing it hidden in one of the bookcases.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: If you look carefully you may find them, and they may be of some use to you.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: I really can't be any more help than that I'm afraid, it is more than my job's worth to have given you the help I already have.

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.player: Okay, thanks a lot, you've been very helpful!

the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.speaker: Miss Cheevers
the-tests-miss-cheevers-talking-to-miss-.text: Best of luck with the test [player name], I hope your application is successful.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.player: Hello there. What am I supposed to be doing in this room?

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: Well, your task is to take this fox, this chicken and this bag of grain across that bridge there to the other side of the room.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: When you have done that, your task is complete.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: Well, it is not quite as simple as that may sound.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: Firstly, you may only carry one of the objects across the room at a time, for the bridge is old and fragile.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: Secondly, the fox wants to eat the chicken, and the chicken wants to eat the grain. Should you ever leave the fox unattended with the chicken, or the grain unattended with the chicken, then

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.text: one of them will be eaten, and you will be unable to complete the test.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-entering-the-room.player: Okay, I'll see what I can do.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.player: Listen, this is really annoying me. Can't you just stop the fox eating the chicken or the chicken eating the grain for me, while I carry the other stuff across the bridge?

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.text: I am afraid not, [player name]. My task is solely to observe your progress, we have explicit instructions not to assist you in any way..

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.player: No, but seriously, please? Think of the poor chicken and grain! Being eaten!

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.text: I am truly sorry, but my hands are tied. I suggest you think carefully before taking any items across the bridge with you, to ensure nothing gets eaten while you are not paying attention.

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.text: This is the only help I may give you...

the-tests-sir-spishyus-attempting-to-cro.player: I really don't think I should be carrying more than 5 Kg across that rickety bridge...

the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.speaker: Sir Spishyus
the-tests-sir-spishyus-talking-to-sir-sp.text: No... I am very sorry. Apparently you are not up to the challenge. I will return you where you came from, better luck in the future.

finishing-up.player: I believe I've managed to pass the tests!

finishing-up.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
finishing-up.text: Oh, jolly well done! Your performance will need to be evaluated by Sir Vey personally, but I don't think it's going too far ahead of myself to welcome you to the team!
Your respawn point has been left alone, but you can now speak to Sir Tiffy to change it to Falador.
